reply_text:
The pinned Mathlib is six months old (29 March). I'm cloning current Mathlib next to it, just for searching:Good call. The pinned Mathlib is from 29 March, six months old. Current Mathlib is now cloned at `/home/joe/code/mathlib4-latest` (28 September). I compared the two for the gaps the loops keep naming:

**Newer Mathlib has:**
- **Singular homology invariance under homotopy**, plus H₀ (`AlgebraicTopology/SingularHomology/HomotopyInvariance*.lean`, `HomologyZero.lean`). topo2's homology problems build this kind of machinery by hand, so it could save real work.
- **Submersions and immersions of manifolds** (`Geometry/Manifold/Submersion.lean`, `ImmersionDiff.lean`). These match t97A07's regular-point conditions and t95A04's immersion.
- **A little more on integral curves and Picard–Lindelöf.** That's the area of t92J08's stall, though I haven't checked whether it covers the uniform-in-a-neighbourhood version it needs.

**Still missing:** the inverse function theorem on manifolds, which is t99J04's stall. So t99J04 still has to build it. The newer Mathlib doesn't help there.

**I'd keep the pin and use the new copy for searching and porting.** Moving the project up would mean going from Lean v4.29 to v4.35, and the new Mathlib uses Lean's newer module system (`public import`). Every problem file and `ConstructionTargets` module would need migrating while both loops are running. Porting only the declarations a route needs into `ConstructionTargets` costs far less. It keeps the source citation, and it doesn't touch the 61 closed proofs.

I've written this rule into `TOPOLOGY-ROUTES.md` (f48263de): before building a missing notion, grep the new copy, and if it's there, port it.

The three seats looking for new routes were briefed before this, so they don't know about the new copy. When their routes come back, I'll check any "build X" step against it before adding it as work.

The t95J02 test also compiles for me (exit 0, no `sorry`). Committing it the same way:All three re-routes are back. Two are now topo1 work rows, and the third is being corrected.

| Problem | Seat | Test at our pinned Mathlib | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| t91J06 | topo-9 | compiles, no `sorry` (rechecked by me) | open topo1 row (293cd571) |
| t95J02 | topo-10 | compiles, no `sorry` (rechecked by me) | open topo1 row (6b3d27de) |
| t99J04 | topo-11 | **fails**: 2 errors | topo-11 is fixing it; not yet queued |

**t95J02, the Klein bottle problem.** The old route stalled trying to classify which points of the gluing relation are equivalent.
- **The new route** lifts the formula (x,y) ↦ (cos 2πy, sin 2πy · cos πx) to the Klein bottle. That gives a continuous map, which serves directly as the inverse coordinate on the vertical circle, so the classification is never needed.
- **The rest** is a homotopy for the glide, then the H₁ argument using results already in the corpus.
- topo-10 rates its confidence at 0.8.
- **The new topo1 row** covers steps 1–4, which remove one of the three `sorry`s. Step 5 is small and independent, and the row allows it once steps 1–4 land.

The t91J06 route is the clamp-and-ramp formula I described last time.

**t99J04:** its route (compose the chart maps as local homeomorphisms, then build the diffeomorphism from its fields) looks sound. I'm holding it until its test compiles at our Mathlib version, and I'm still parked on topo-11's fix. topo1 is working the refill problems meanwhile; it's on t98A06 part (a) now. The two new rows are open in its worklist, but they don't jump the queue, so topo1 will take them when its election reaches them.
